payload.reason: The authors suggest that Twitter data provides better predictions about language use because it captures a wider range of languages, especially in regions with sparse ground-truth data, and avoids biases associated with language-specific searches.

claims.text: Twitter has fewer missing languages compared to other corpora, providing a better representation of language use in countries with limited ground-truth data.
Twitter data matches populations better when weighted by GDP, indicating it represents wealthier populations more accurately than general web-crawled data.
The method of collecting Twitter data without language-specific searches helps avoid biases, leading to a more accurate representation of language use.
